text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: ALERT fired for service=redd-ml-inference (Severity: high). Trigger: 95th percentile latency > 1.5s for 2m. Incident URL: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: notification sent to primary on-call @Alex K. If not acknowledged within 2m, will escalate to secondary then manager per policy `redwood-prod-escalation`.

Alex K: acked. Looking now. seeing increased tail latency on pods serving long-context requests. I’ll take the initial triage. :eyes:

Alex K: looks like one of the inference nodes lost connection to redis K-V cache, ~30% increased token times on that shard. Re-routing traffic away from pod-7 makes P50 better. Trying quick drain.

Devon T: @Alex K nice catch. Can you run the scale-up script while you drain? I can patch routing if needed.

Alex K: running scale with `./ops/scale.sh redd-ml-serving +2` (eta 45s).

incident-bot: PagerDuty: primary acknowledgement window expired for secondary; escalating to secondary @Lina G.

Lina G: on my way, getting pinged but mobile DND right now, give me 30s. Trying to switch to desktop. :phone:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: escalation triggered to manager @Sarah M (secondary and on-call did not fully acknowledge within policy window). Please join the bridge if available.

Sarah M: I'm awake, joining. Oncall summary?

Alex K: TL;DR: single inference host lost redis conn -> degraded batch merging -> higher tail latency -> some 504s from gateway. Drain + scale started, traffic being rebalanced. Impact: intermittent 504s for long-sequence customers, estimate 7% of production requests in last 3m. No data exfiltration.

Sarah M: Good. Devs, if scaling/drain doesn't stabilize in 2m we'll fallback traffic to `redd-ml-legacy` versions and flip canary routing. Prepare rollback play.

Devon T: patching routing now: applying immediate route weight change to deprioritize pod-7 and push traffic to warm pool. Command I ran:

```
kubectl patch svc redd-ml-svc -p '{"spec": {"traffic": [{"subset":"warm","weight":80},{"subset":"primary","weight":20}]}}'
```

Alex K: scale finished, new pods initializing. Logs show redis reconnect flapping on node 7; I'm cordoning it: `kubectl cordon pod-7 && kubectl delete pod pod-7`

incident-bot: PagerDuty: manager escalation acknowledged by Sarah M.

Sarah M: Thanks. I'm monitoring SLIs. Lina, when you're fully back please confirm whether mobile DND suppressed PD push; we should track this for followup.

Lina G: confirmed — my phone suppressed the push; I had a low-power profile that blocked notifications. Filing a follow-up with oncall config team after incident.

Alex K: after drain + scale + routing change, 95th latency back under 1.1s, 504s dropped to near-zero. Gateway error logs still show a small tail for requests >8k tokens, but overall healthy.

Sarah M: customer impact assessment: Affected sessions were long-context batch jobs for ~15 customers; estimated total requests impacted ~1200 in last 8m, majority recovered via retries. No SLA credits decision yet — waiting for full request replay and error budget calc.

Devon T: one action item: add redis connection circuit breaker to serving runtime to fail fast earlier and avoid batch pile-ups. I'll file a ticket and come back with ETA.

Sarah M: Agreed. Also add a PD rule tweak: notify secondary via SMS even when mobile DND present for 2nd-level escalations. Lina please own follow-up. :memo:

Lina G: will do. Creating follow-up issue with logs + PD delivery detail.

Alex K: closing on-call actions: pod-7 replaced, traffic stable, temp mitigation in place. I'll keep monitoring for 15m then hand back to normal ops.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for now — no ongoing paging. If metrics regress, PagerDuty will re-fire. :white_check_mark:
